svg.title: Split each such tested spectral integral into E ≤1 with transverse frequencies inside the box widened by λ, and its complement. On the complement, the Schwartz bound of order k gives an arbitrary factor λ−k in a transverse direction. For E > 1 the actual exterior time gap gives e−E/λw; for every fixed R, M this is at most λ−Me−RE, eventually. The finite damped moments from (RT3) then pay the whole complement. Inside the box use (RT2) with the two reciprocal weights from (RT7) for shear components, and (RT7),(RT9) for a diagonal component. Split the latter once more at E = λ−3000. Below that threshold (including zero), the large gain in the line estimate pays a crude stress bound; above it (RT9) applies. With the stated widths these estimates, including the primitive amplitude λ100, leave a bound Cλ−1. Thus the exterior flux tends to zero.
